{{no footnotes|date=November 2012}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''system of bilinear equations''' is a special sort of [[system of polynomial equations]], where each equation equates a [[bilinear form]] with a constant (possibly zero). More precisely, given two sets of variables represented as [[coordinate vector]]s {{math|''x''}} and ''y'', then each equation of the system can be written  <math display=block>y^TA_ix=g_i,</math> where, {{math|''i''}} is an [[integer]] whose value ranges from 1 to the number of equations, each <math>A_i</math> is a [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]], and each <math>g_i</math> is a [[real number]]. Systems of bilinear equations arise in many subjects including [[engineering]], [[biology]], and [[statistics]].
